text:
incident-bot: SEV P1: multiple model-warmup failures in us-west-2 — OOMs and CUDA driver errors detected. Paging oncall (primary: sanjay). Auto-attach logs: /var/log/warmup/*.log :alert:

sanjay: got the page, looking now. any affected customer lists?

maria: seeing repeated deserialization errors followed by compile timeouts on the warmup workers. stack: `llm-warmup:v4` nodes. sample log:
```
ERROR warmup: model_deserialize failed: malloc failed: out of memory
CUDA error: out of memory (driver 456.71)
compile: timeout after 120s while building attention kernel
``` 

alex: also node-flap on node gw-usw2-42 around 14:02 UTC — kubelet restarted, containers OOMKilled. CPU fine, mem spike during `model.load()`

sanjay: first mitigation: reduce warmup concurrency on node pool to 1 and disable background prefetch. running command now: `kubectl patch cm warmup-config -p '{"data":{"concurrency":"1","prefetch":"false"}}'`

lena: notif to impacted customers? Product says we should soft notify accounts with active dedicated capacity and high qps. recommend "temporary degraded warmup" msg.

maria: disabling compile cache flush for this run — we suspect a corrupt cached artifact causing compile storm. command: `rm -rf /var/cache/compile/*` on warmup nodes + restart warmup pods. doing rollout.

eng-ops-bot: rollout started for warmup jobset `warmup-workers-v4` (12 pods) — 3 at a time. ETA ~6m. :gear:

sanjay: good. also enabling fallback routing to `redwood-small-quant` for new requests to keep latency stable. patching router: `route-policy set fallback=redwood-small-quant for model-family=v4`

alex: noticed one worker doing repeated `dlopen` failures before OOM. possible artifact corruption on disk. checked checksum: mismatch on /artifacts/v4/weights.bin

maria: copying artifact from s3 to node for one test: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/v4/weights.bin /tmp/` then `sha256sum` matches remote. suspect intermittent EBS read issues.

sanjay: okay, plan:
- pause warmup prefetch + concurrency=1 (done)
- restart affected nodes after drain (scheduled)
- clear compile cache (in progress)
- enable fallback model routing (done)
- notify customers with potential degraded warmup

lena: drafting customer note, short and technical: "We detected model warmup failures causing delays for some model-initial requests in us-west-2. We have enabled fallback routes and are restarting warmup workers. No inference correctness impact."

maria: after clearing caches and restarting pods, observed fewer OOMs but still occasional compile timeout at 14:12 UTC. increasing compile timeout to 300s for these models while we stabilize: `CONFIG_COMPILE_TIMEOUT=300` and re-deploy.

alex: node restarts complete for gw-usw2-42 and gw-usw2-43. memory pressure normalized. one pod still OOMKilled twice — collecting core from /var/crash.

sanjay: handing off primary oncall to tz-asia-oncall for overnight coverage — I’ll stay available for questions. handoff note: "warmup OOMs in us-west-2 caused by artifact checksum mismatch + compile timeouts. mitigations: reduced concurrency, cleared compile cache, fallback routing, increased compile timeout. Monitor for 1 hour."

tz-asia-oncall: acknowledged. I'll watch the warmup dashboard and alert if error rate >5% for 10m. please put any customer comms in #customer-impact.

eng-ops-bot: Canary alert: warmup-error-rate dropped from 18% -> 4.6% over the last 8 minutes after mitigation. :chart_with_downwards_trend:

maria: follow-up: we've identified a flaky EBS volume that returns partial reads under load. migrating artifacts to a different volume group and replacing the node disk images. ops ticket created: OPS-1427.

sanjay: assigning post-incident tasks: (1) artifact integrity check at boot (2) increase compile timeout heuristics for large models (3) autoscale warmup pool on artifact read latency (4) run full load test for v4 on new disk images.

lena: customer comm posted to #customer-impact and sent to accounts team for outbound to high-QPS customers. tone: transparent, technical, and guidance included.

tz-asia-oncall: continuing watch. if error rate goes above 6% I'll escalate to eng-runtime oncall. keeping this thread pinned. :pushpin:

maria: adding logs and traces to incident doc: link: https://redwood-incidents/6865432100 (will fill after shift)

sanjay: thanks team. leaving note in pager duty: warmup OOMs (mitigated) — handoff to tz-asia-oncall at 14:25 UTC. will follow up on OPS-1427 tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigations applied, severity downgraded to P2. timeline saved.
